newsitem.title: UK: UK govt N Irish fish pledge raises its vote hopes.
newsitem.headline: UK govt N Irish fish pledge raises its vote hopes.

text.p: A Northern Irish legislator said on Monday he had won a pledge from Britain's government of help for the province's trawlermen, making it more likely that the government will win a crucial parliamentary vote.
John Taylor, deputy leader of the nine-strong Ulster Unionist parliamentary party, has been campaigning for extra fishing quotas for the province's fishermen.
He says they lose out from the European Union's fishing policy to their Irish Republic counterparts.

Taylor said in a statement: "At last I now have a letter from the government to assure the Ulster fish industry that the Conservative government will use international quota swaps to benefit Ulster fishermen."
Taylor did not say specifically that this breakthrough would persuade his party not to vote against the government in a division at 2200 GMT on the EU's fishing policy.
But he added: "The Labour Party can only get our support if they in turn support our local fishing industry. That is not clear so far."

The government could need at least the abstention of Ulster Unionists if it is to win the vote since it has no overall majority in parliament and may not be backed by all Conservative Eurosceptic MPs.
If it loses, Labour might put down a motion of no confidence in the government. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
